sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 12.8% a year from $4,860.4 million in FY2016 to $14,342.9 million in FY2025 [F1][F10][F198], but the path was a step change rather than a smooth climb.

FY2021 revenue jumped 89.1% to $16,071.7 million [F6][D241], driven by REGEN-COV US sales of $5,828.0 million that contributed 66.4pp of growth [S48][D582], and FY2022 then fell 24.3% to $12,172.9 million as REGEN-COV went to zero [F7][D292][S49][D585].
Operating margin peaked at 55.7% in FY2021 [F26][D750] and has fallen every year since, to 24.9% in FY2025, a 30.7pp decline over four years [F30][R1].

The last three years show the underlying business: revenue grew at a 5.6% three-year CAGR [D767] while operating income fell at an 8.9% CAGR [D769], so the post-pandemic base is growing more slowly than the top line suggests.

The growth engine has shifted from EYLEA to collaboration profit shares: US EYLEA was 63.0% of revenue in FY2017 [D554] but only 19.2% in FY2025 [D576], while collaboration revenue reached 51.1% of revenue in FY2025 [D521].

In FY2025 US EYLEA sales fell 42.4% to $2,747.8 million, a 14.2pp drag on growth [S43][D577][D578], while Regeneron's share of Sanofi antibody profits rose 33.6% to $5,241.6 million and added 9.3pp [S52][D591][D592].

The EYLEA decline came from lower sales volumes on competitive pressure, share loss to compounded bevacizumab and the transition to EYLEA HD, plus a lower net selling price [P10], while EYLEA HD rose on higher volumes partly offset by a lower price [P11].
The profit-share increase was driven by higher profits primarily associated with an increase in Dupixent sales [P9].

Operating costs grew 5.4% against 1.0% revenue growth in FY2025 [D457][D440], a 4.4pp gap [D464], so there was no operating leverage; net income still rose 2.1% [D442] and diluted EPS 8.2% [D444] as the diluted share count fell 5.6% [D459].
The FY2025 operating margin of 24.9% is the window low, 9.7pp below the 34.6% median and 30.8pp below the FY2021 high [F30][D749][D751][D750].
The FY2025 bridge is almost entirely R&D: R&D rose 14.0% and cost 4.7pp of margin [D455][D465], SG&A fell 8.6% and added 2.0pp [D456][D466], and other lines took 0.5pp [D467].
The SG&A decline was primarily due to lower charitable contributions to Good Days, partly offset by about $60 million of fourth-quarter matching donations [P5].
R&D was 40.8% of revenue in FY2025 [D420], against a 34.6% window median [D760] and a 20.1% peer median, the highest in the eight-company peer group [D779][D778].
Below the line, other income of $1,652.8 million [X117] held net margin at 31.4% [F50], 6.5pp above the 24.9% operating margin [F30], even as the effective tax rate rose to 13.9% [D427].
Operating cash flow of $4,978.9 million was 1.11x net income in FY2025 [F80][F40][D428], while free cash flow was 0.91x net income [D429], against a 0.88x window median for that ratio [D763].
Free cash flow was $4,080.5 million, a 28.4% margin [F100][D425], with capex of $898.4 million at 6.3% of revenue and 1.65x D&A [F90][D424][D430].

Capex has been running for the Tarrytown campus and Rensselaer fill/finish expansion, with management guiding $825 million to $950 million for 2024 and continued significant spending thereafter [P19].
Stock-based compensation of $993.7 million equalled 20.0% of operating cash flow [X77][D431], so cash earnings lean on a non-cash add-back.
Cash and investments reached $18,865.8 million against $1,985.9 million of debt, for net cash of $16,879.9 million, or 117.7% of revenue [D432][F187][D434][D435].

That net cash ratio is the 100th percentile of the eight-company peer group, whose median is -50.7% of revenue [D780][D781], and the current ratio of 4.13x sits above its 3.97x window median [F180][D766].
FY2025 buybacks of $3,438.6 million plus a first dividend of $370.3 million came to $3,808.9 million, 93.3% of free cash flow [X137][X140][D436][D437], and the diluted share count fell 5.6% [D459].
Return on average equity fell to 14.9% [D439], the 25th percentile against a 38.7% peer median [D784][D785], as the equity base grew faster than earnings.
The four-year, 30.7pp operating-margin slide is the main flag [R1][F26][F30]: it reflects a deliberate R&D build against a shrinking EYLEA base, and the FY2025 margin is now the window low [D749].

The revenue basis break matters for any long-window comparison: FY2018 is shown as $5,145.6 million against $6,710.8 million first reported, and FY2019 as $6,557.6 million against $7,863.4 million [R2][F3][X3][F4][X4], so growth rates spanning those years mix two presentations.
The FY2021 R&D and FY2020 receivables recasts are small and do not change any conclusion here [R3][X30][R4][X192].
Whether the operating margin holds above the FY2025 low of 24.9% [F30][D749]; a further decline would confirm the four-year trend, and the FY2026 10-K will show it.
Whether US EYLEA sales stabilize above the FY2025 level of $2,747.8 million [S43] as EYLEA HD, at $1,636.9 million [S64], offsets the decline; the FY2026 10-K segment table will show it.
Whether R&D as a share of revenue falls back below the 40.8% FY2025 level [D420] toward the 34.6% window median [D760]; the FY2026 10-K income statement will show it.

Whether buybacks plus dividends stay near the 93.3% of free cash flow seen in FY2025 [D437]; a move above that level would mean the balance sheet is funding the return, and the FY2026 10-K cash flow statement will show it.
